content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I've been working with the logger Excel file shared in one of the forum threads. I've translated parts of it to English to help others.
Here you go, my apologies for the delay.
Just a quick note: you can't use both the [product_name] software and the logger at the same time.

Thanks! This works well—except for one issue. I'm unable to log digital flag states. I have two flags (M1 and M2). If I enter M01 in the header, the value is always 0, even if the flag is 1. If I use M1 as named in the software, the cell stays empty. Any advice?
I'll investigate this further and update you by the weekend.

That sounds perfect, thank you. I've tried another file from the forum but it crashes after about 30 minutes. I suspected my computer setup was the issue, but your file runs smoothly for several days straight. It would be even better if I could log flag statuses too. Regards [user_name]
[user_name], I've fixed the flag logging issue and the logger should now work. Please check the updated version.
Good afternoon all, I used the data logger on an analog project and it recorded percentage values correctly. Next, I plan to experiment with temperature logging.
Sorry for another update—I added a reset button to the logger. You can now reset to row 11 with a single click. [user_name]

Hello again, thank you for your work. Unfortunately, I still can't log flag statuses. I've attached my project for review. In the bottom right corner, two flags (M1 and M2) indicate valve status for my solar heating setup: one shows if the valve is open, the other closed. Both M01 and M02 always display '0' in the logger file. Am I using the wrong IDs?
[user_name], Try this logger version instead. It should work.
Hello everyone, I've updated the data logger so it can now record both date/time, analog values, and digital flags, clear cell contents, and reset to cell 11. I hope this helps. [user_name]

[user_name], That's what this forum is for—helping each other. [user_name] ([user_name])
Great job, thank you for sharing this excellent logger.

Hi [user_name], Can I get your expert opinion on these two points? 1) If I connect a GPRS modem to the [product_name] module via the programming port, which creates a VPN back to a similar modem on a PC, could the Excel logger work over such a channel, or would there be timing issues? 2) If another GPRS modem with local code performs similar port polling as the Excel logger (using VBA script, but instead in Java), extracts data from the [product_name], then sends it as TCP/IP packets to another system (like an OPC server), could this data be used in a SCADA setup? I'm exploring technical possibilities—thanks for your insights. I believe the VBA script behind the logger could be re-written in a different environment to enable new data extraction methods. Has anyone managed to send info back to the [product_name] besides Run/Stop? Some modems offer on-board programming and digital I/O that can be triggered by SMS, which could also be wired to the [product_name] inputs as with the INSYS module. I appreciate your perspective! Thanks Aaaaaarrrrggghhh! ("Have a nice day!")

[user_name], I'm not a VB expert. My logger was created through a lot of online research and Microsoft help files. As for modems, I haven't dealt with communication for [product_name] modules before. Perhaps someone with deeper VB expertise can assist. Sorry [user_name] ([user_name])
[user_name], Thank you for your honest reply.

Hello [user_name], Let me answer your questions: 1) The Excel logger should also work with modem or GSM connections. The Insys module operates in a similar way. GPRS may introduce delays due to IP network latency, but VB can adjust for this timing. 2) You can develop your own software to read out [product_name] data; it's not complicated. The original logger software was DOS-based and written in Turbo Pascal. I've used a programmable serial-IP converter (see [url]) to display data on web pages; programming is done in an object-oriented basic dialect. If interested, I can upload it online. It should be straightforward to convert the Excel VB script to another language.
I'm interested—please share.

Hi [user_name], The [product_name] Logger is still under development. It's stable for short-term logging but unstable for prolonged use. On my PC (Windows XP), it's fine, but other users report instability. You can only read certain values—outputs can't be changed. The new [product_name] version with SD card logging might be a better solution, as it doesn't require a PC.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are utilizing a custom data logger for [product_name] modules to monitor automation tasks such as solar heating control. The logger successfully captures analog values but struggles with accurately recording the status of digital markers, displaying either zeros or leaving fields blank. The community is actively working to resolve this, with updates including new features like a reset button. A recurring issue is that users can't run the official [product_name] software and the logger simultaneously. Discussions also involve extending functionality, like remote logging via modems, and converting logger scripts to other programming languages to support alternative communication methods.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the logger to reliably record both analog and digital data, especially digital marker states for automated devices, and to support concurrent usage with the official [product_name] software.
